transcript:
Jordan (Redwood AE) [00:00]: hey everyone, thanks for joining, hopefully the audio is okay. we got about 45 minutes, um quick roll call?
Samira (Redwood SE) [00:12]: hey all, samira here. i'll take notes on infra items.
Priya (NexaHealth) [00:18]: priya, thanks. i have ethan and maya with me.
Ethan (NexaHealth) [00:22]: hey team. quick heads up, we might have to hop off at 15:40 for another meeting.
Liam (Redwood CSM) [00:26]: noted, quick agenda then: onboarding progress, access, network, bench plan, next steps.
---
Jordan [02:10]: repro the status — priya, last week we were waiting on service account + the VPC peering details? where are we on that?
Priya [02:28]: yes, we had a delay with security. ethan is on it, right ethan?
Ethan [02:35]: yeah, took a bit longer. we now have a ticket, working with infra to create an RBAC role. i'll need the exact IAM perms that redwood needs, an exact list.
Samira [02:48]: perfect, i'll paste the minimal iam perms into the checklist. in general we need s3:GetObject for the test data location, kms:Decrypt if you're using CMKs, and the api key/service account to call the hosted pilot endpoints.
Maya [03:05]: sorry quick q, do we need full list or can we do a temporary elevated role? security prefers least privilege so temporary is fine but we'll need specifics.
Samira [03:16]: least privilege is ideal, we'll send the checklist with exact perms. we'll also include an option for a service account you create versus us creating a service account in our project.
Jordan [03:27]: also, regarding S3 encryption, if you're using customer-managed keys, we need the key policy to allow the service account decrypt. we'll document that.
---
Samira [07:00]: on network, we saw the VPC peering pre-reqs — priya can you confirm your CIDR blocks? we need them for the peering request.
Priya [07:12]: yep, it's 10.10.0.0/16 for our pilot VPC. i'll put that into the ticket.
Ethan [07:20]: and we have a corporate firewall that might block some outbound ranges, any specific IPs we should whitelist?
Samira [07:28]: yes, we'll send a short list — the control plane endpoints and the inference egress IPs. i'll include tcp/443 and the port ranges for websocket streaming.
Jordan [08:05]: note — if peering isn't allowed by security, we can fall back to a cross-account S3 pattern and signed URLs, but that has small latency tradeoffs.
Maya [08:18]: hmm that may be okay if latency stays under 200ms for our calls. what's been typical for similar customers?
Samira [08:27]: for 2k token contexts with our dedicated pools we often see steady-state latencies around 80-180ms per token chunk depending on batching, but cross-account signed URLs add ~20-80ms variance.
---
Jordan [12:40]: let's talk data — any updates on the anonymized sample dataset?
Maya [12:47]: i'm prepping it; i have a subset of 5k records going to an encrypted s3. question on format: do you want jsonl with prompt/response or csv?
Samira [12:58]: jsonl with prompt/metadata is best; include a 'gold_response' field where possible. that helps the quality checks.
Maya [13:08]: got it, will upload by friday. link will be shared to the shared drive.
Ethan [13:18]: about keys — do you want an access key that is scoped to the bucket or role-based?
Samira [13:24]: role-based service account is preferred; less key management. we'll include both options in the checklist.
---
Jordan [18:02]: benchmarks — goal is to run a latency + throughput run after access is ready. plan = run baseline hosted model, then run with dedicated pool if we can. priya any uptime windows we should avoid for the run?
Priya [18:18]: prefer off-hours, but the pilot test window of 10/26-10/30 looks good.
Jordan [18:26]: great. we'll aim to schedule bench on monday 10/26. samira, can you lead the run and collect the logs?
Samira [18:34]: yes — i'll prepare a small harness, we'll need a test script from maya that simulates your typical 2k prompt flow, also please include concurrency targets.
Maya [18:45]: concurrency usually 12 workers at peak for our microservice. i'll give you a script.
---
Ethan [22:50]: small issue — we tried to curl the control plane and got a TLS error, might be on our side.
Samira [23:02]: can you paste the exact curl? also check SNI and SSO proxies; some corporate proxies rewrite TLS.
Ethan [23:10]: yeah, sending in chat: 'curl https://api.redwood.example/v1/health' returned 'tls: handshake error'.
Samira [23:20]: okay that often means the outbound proxy requires cert pinning or mutual TLS; we can support mTLS for Private installs but for hosted API you may need the proxy to allow the endpoint. do you have a proxy log?
Ethan [23:30]: i'll check, but security tends to block unknown CNs.
Jordan [23:45]: follow up: if proxy is in the path we can provide a list of CNs and also provide an alternative option — use a Bastion jump or run the benchmark from a cloud staging instance we provision for you.
Priya [24:02]: provisioned staging would be easiest for the bench run, less dependent on corp firewall.
---
Liam [30:00]: quick commercial items — jordan, any updates on pilot pricing?
Jordan [30:10]: i updated the pilot pricing sheet; main change is we added a burst buffer for the dedicated run and a fixed monthly pilot fee. i'll send the sheet after call.
Priya [30:20]: do we need to sign an MSA for the pilot?
Jordan [30:24]: not for the basic pilot, we'll do a pilot agreement + SLA; i've flagged a short form MSA for enterprise later.
---
Maya [33:40]: one more technical — tokenization, do you have a tokenizer tool to estimate token counts for our datasets? we've seen weird token counts with other vendors.
Samira [33:52]: yes, we can share a tokenizer script that mirrors the model's BPE. we'll include that in the repo. generally count depends on punctuation and language — share a sample and we can pre-tokenize.
Maya [34:08]: great. that helps cost estimates too.
---
Ethan [37:50]: security question — we need Redwood to provide SOC2 cert and audit logs retention policy for pilot. where's that doc?
Liam [38:02]: we have a security pack — i'll share SOC2 summary, ISO certs, data retention and audit logs. expect link in email after call.
Ethan [38:10]: perfect. also SSO: we might do SAML later, pilot can use api keys?
Jordan [38:18]: api keys ok for pilot, for long-term we support SAML/SSO, SCIM provisioning.
---
Priya [41:30]: recap?
Jordan [41:35]: recap: samira sends integration checklist + firewall ips by 10/21; ethan to create RBAC service account or allow us scoped access by 10/22; maya to upload anonymized jsonl data by 10/22; jordan sends pilot pricing + SLA doc by 10/20; schedule bench for week of 10/26 — samira to run.
Priya [41:58]: all good, thanks everyone.
Samira [42:05]: i'll also add the curl troubleshooting steps and provide an alternate staging host to avoid proxy issues.
Jordan [42:12]: ok we'll follow up in writing, sending minutes + links. thanks all.
---
(End of recording)
